results.q: What happens when a message is posted to a queue that is already full?
answer: This is handled in OSQPost() (Source/os_q.c:672): it checks `pq->OSQEntries >= pq->OSQSize`, and when that is true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and returns `(OS_ERR_Q_FULL)`, so the rest of OSQPost() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when a task asks for a memory block and the partition has none left?
answer: This is decided in OSMemGet() (Source/os_mem.c:197): it checks `pmem->OSMemNFree > 0u`; when that is NOT true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and reports `*perr = OS_ERR_MEM_NO_FREE_BLKS` to its caller and returns `((void *)0)`, so the rest of OSMemGet() is skipped.
Bad input is also rejected in other places: OSMemCreate() drops it when `nblks < 2u` (Source/os_mem.c:110), counting it in OSMemCreate.perr.

results.q: What happens when a task waiting on a semaphore times out?
answer: The timeout is detected where the status is set: OSEventPendMulti() sets `OSTCBCur->OSTCBStatPend = OS_STAT_PEND_TO` (Source/os_core.c:503); OSTimeTick() sets `ptcb->OSTCBStatPend = OS_STAT_PEND_TO` (Source/os_core.c:992) when `ptcb->OSTCBDly == 0u` and `(ptcb->OSTCBStat & OS_STAT_PEND_ANY) != OS_STAT_RDY`; OSTimeDlyResume() sets `ptcb->OSTCBStatPend = OS_STAT_PEND_TO` (Source/os_time.c:205) when `(ptcb->OSTCBStat & OS_STAT_PEND_ANY) != OS_STAT_RDY`.

The waiting code then handles it in OSSemPend() (Source/os_sem.c:377): it switches on `OSTCBCur->OSTCBStatPend`, and in the case `OS_STAT_PEND_TO` / `default` (line 387) it calls OS_EventTaskRemove() and calls OS_EventTaskRemove() and reports `*perr = OS_ERR_TIMEOUT` to its caller.

results.q: What happens when a task is created at a priority that is already taken?
answer: This is decided in OSTaskCreate() (Source/os_task.c:249): it checks `OSTCBPrioTbl[prio] == (OS_TCB *)0`; when that is NOT true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and returns `(OS_ERR_PRIO_EXIST)`, so the rest of OSTaskCreate() is skipped.

Bad input is also rejected in other places: OSMutexCreate() drops it when `prio != OS_PRIO_MUTEX_CEIL_DIS` (Source/os_mutex.c:225), counting it in OSTCBPrioTbl, OSMutexCreate.perr; OSTaskNameGet() drops it when `ptcb == OS_TCB_RESERVED` (Source/os_task.c:733), counting it in OSTaskNameGet.perr; OSTaskNameSet() drops it when `ptcb == OS_TCB_RESERVED` (Source/os_task.c:814), counting it in OSTaskNameSet.perr.

results.q: What happens when there are no free task control blocks left?
answer: This is decided in OS_TCBInit() (Source/os_core.c:2046): it checks `ptcb != (OS_TCB *)0`; when that is NOT true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and returns `(OS_ERR_TASK_NO_MORE_TCB)`, so the rest of OS_TCBInit() is skipped.
Its caller OSTaskCreate() checks `err == OS_ERR_NONE` (Source/os_task.c:255) and then calls OS_Sched() and calls OS_Sched().
Its caller OSTaskCreateExt() checks `err == OS_ERR_NONE` (Source/os_task.c:393) and then calls OS_Sched() and calls OS_Sched().
Bad input is also rejected in other places: OSMemGet() drops it when `!(pmem->OSMemNFree > 0u)` (Source/os_mem.c:197), counting it in OSMemGet.perr.

results.q: What happens when OSSemPend is called from an ISR?
answer: This is handled in OSSemPend() (Source/os_sem.c:351): it checks `OSIntNesting > 0u`, and when that is true it reports `*perr = OS_ERR_PEND_ISR` to its caller and returns immediately, so the rest of OSSemPend() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: CPU_CRITICAL_ENTER, CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT — the previous values stay in place.

results.q: What happens when a task waits for a mutex that a lower-priority task owns?
answer: This is handled in OSMutexAccept() (Source/os_mutex.c:126): it checks `(pevent->OSEventCnt & OS_MUTEX_KEEP_LOWER_8) == OS_MUTEX_AVAILABLE`, and when that is true it sets `pevent->OSEventCnt &= OS_MUTEX_KEEP_UPPER_8` (line 127); then it sets `pevent->OSEventCnt |= (INT16U)OSTCBCur->OSTCBPrio` (line 128); then it sets `pevent->OSEventPtr = (void *)OSTCBCur` (line 129); then it checks `(pcp != OS_PRIO_MUTEX_CEIL_DIS) && (OSTCBCur->OSTCBPrio <= pcp)` (line 130); if true it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and sets `*perr = OS_ERR_PCP_LOWER`; then it calls CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT (line 135); then it sets `*perr = OS_ERR_NONE` (line 136); then it returns `(OS_TRUE)`, so the rest of OSMutexAccept() is skipped.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT — the previous values stay in place.

Consequence: OSMboxPost() checks `pevent->OSEventPtr != (void *)0` (Source/os_mbox.c:553); `pevent->OSEventPtr != (void *)0` depends on runtime values, so it may return early, skipping CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and may call CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and may call CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT.

Consequence: OSMboxPostOpt() checks `pevent->OSEventPtr != (void *)0` (Source/os_mbox.c:640); `pevent->OSEventPtr != (void *)0` depends on runtime values, so it may return early, skipping CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and may call CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT and may call CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT.
Consequence: OSEventPendMulti() checks `pevent->OSEventCnt > 0u` (Source/os_core.c:414); `pevent->OSEventCnt > 0u` depends on runtime values, so it may return early, skipping CPU_CRITICAL_EXIT.

Bad input is also rejected in other places: OSMutexPend() drops it when `(INT8U)(pevent->OSEventCnt & OS_MUTEX_KEEP_LOWER_8) == OS_MUTEX_AVAILABLE` (Source/os_mutex.c:517), counting it in os_event.OSEventPtr, os_event.OSEventCnt; OSMutexCreate() drops it when `prio != OS_PRIO_MUTEX_CEIL_DIS` (Source/os_mutex.c:225), counting it in OSTCBPrioTbl, OSMutexCreate.perr; OSTaskNameGet() drops it when `prio > OS_LOWEST_PRIO` (Source/os_task.c:708), counting it in OSTaskNameGet.perr.

results.q: Where is the system time OSTime incremented?
answer: OSTime is a global variable of type `volatile INT32U`, defined in Source/ucos_ii.h:760 — the code describes it as: "Current value of system time (in ticks)".
It is set by OSTimeTick() (`OSTime++`, line 954); OS_InitMisc() (`OSTime = 0uL`, line 1392); OSTimeSet() (`OSTime = ticks`, line 276).
It is read by OSTimeTick() (line 954), OSTimeGet() (line 247).

In short: OSTime carries a value produced by OSTimeSet(), OSTimeTick(), OS_InitMisc() and consumed by OSTimeGet(), OSTimeTick(). OSTimeTick() both reads and updates it, so it also keeps state between calls.

results.q: How is the CPU usage percentage computed?
answer: It is written here: `OSCPUUsage = 0u` in OS_TaskStat() (Source/os_core.c:1894); `OSCPUUsage   = (INT8U)usage` in OS_TaskStat() (Source/os_core.c:1921); `OSCPUUsage   = 0u` in OS_TaskStat() (Source/os_core.c:1923); `cpu_sr = 0u` in OSCtxSw() (Ports/Win32/Visual Studio/os_cpu_c.c:766).
The value is computed just before: `usage = 100 - (INT8S)(OSIdleCtrRun / OSIdleCtrMax)` (Source/os_core.c:1919).
